name: Positional Play 4-3-3

slots.why: The sweeper keeper is an extra short passing option and covers the space behind the compact shape.
The inverted wing-back joins the midfield passing structure instead of overlapping into the same channel as the winger.
The ball-playing defender begins attacks with measured passes into the midfield triangle.
The cover defender protects the higher line while his partner distributes; Central Defender (Defend) is the safer alternate.
The support full-back provides the natural width that the inverted left-back does not.
The Carrilero shuttles into the left channel to connect play and protect the space around the inverted wing-back.
The deep-lying playmaker anchors circulation from midfield without vacating the centre.
The Mezzala supports from the right half-space, adding a receiver without becoming a second striker.
The inside forward links inside with the midfield and arrives in the box as a supporting threat.
The attacking winger holds the right touchline and attacks the space created by the Mezzala.
The complete forward links the possession structure and remains a credible presence in the box.

description: A 4-3-3 built around a disciplined central triangle, with a Carrilero protecting the inverted side and a Mezzala supporting the wide attack.
whyGood: It gives technical midfielders clear, complementary jobs and keeps enough players behind the ball to sustain possession after a loss.
whyThisShape: The DLP holds the centre, the Carrilero fills the channel beside the inverted wing-back, and the Mezzala supports the opposite half-space. This creates staggered passing options without asking all three midfielders to run beyond the ball at once.
whenToUse: When you have a composed central organiser, a hard-working channel midfielder, and a technical half-space player; especially against a compact side that must be moved patiently.
whenNotToUse: When your midfield lacks passing security or the opponent can repeatedly isolate the full-backs in wide transition.

instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Use the short connections supplied by the selected midfield and supporting forwards.
instructionRationale.Play Out Of Defence: Use short first-line outlets and midfield connections to start attacks; this asks for secure decisions under pressure.
instructionRationale.Work Ball Into Box: Look for an opening around the penalty area rather than encouraging speculative shots.
instructionRationale.Hold Shape: Retain the available passing structure after a regain rather than forcing an immediate counter.
instructionRationale.Higher Line of Engagement: Engage the build-up earlier, accepting that the forwards need support from the midfield behind them.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Centre Backs: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.More Urgent Pressing: Challenge more often inside the selected engagement zone without making the settled press maximal.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Short Kicks: Start possession through the chosen short outlets instead of routinely contesting a long kick.

keyRequirements: Full-backs comfortable in a positional build-up
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
